# Tests that do not pass in a maintained environment, recorded so CI can tell a
# new fingerprint regression apart from this inherited debt. The Test job in
# .github/workflows/go.yml fails on any failing test that is not listed below,
# and warns when one listed here passes again - prune it then.
#
# None of these is a bug this module introduced. Two shared causes:
#
# 1. Byte-for-byte comparisons against recorded flows. Either the harness forks
#    `openssl s_client`/`s_server` and compares what comes back with testdata
#    recorded with OpenSSL 1.1.1 - checkOpenSSLVersion in handshake_test.go
#    refuses to re-record with anything else - or it replays one of uTLS' own
#    parrot/raw-capture recordings (TestUTLSHandshakeClientParrot*,
#    TestUTLSHandshakeClientFingerprintedSpec*, TestUTLSServerNameIP,
#    TestUTLSEmptyServerName, TestUTLSRemoveSNIExtension,
#    TestUTLSHelloRetryRequest), whose key share the test cannot reproduce
#    either. Current OpenSSL is 3.x, so the reference peer sends different bytes
#    (the TestHandshakeClient*, TestHandshakeServer*, TestHandshakClientSCTs,
#    TestClientKeyUpdate, TestVerifyConnection, TestResumption*/TestServerResumption*
#    families). Go 1.15 removed renegotiation, which is why TestRenegotiate* and
#    TestRenegotiationRejected are here too.
#
# 2. Expired test certificates. testRSACertificate in handshake_test.go is
#    notAfter 2025-01-01 and testECDSACertificate is notAfter 2022-11-20, so every
#    handshake that verifies a chain ends in `remote error: tls: bad certificate`.
#
# TestAESCipherReorderingTLS13 is deliberately absent: it nil-panics and would
# abort the binary mid-run, so the Test job skips it (SKIP_TEST in the workflow)
# rather than record it. That abort is also why this list is longer than the set
# of `--- FAIL:` lines a plain `go test ./...` prints - the tests declared after
# the crasher only become visible once the run is allowed to finish.
#
# Recorded 2026-10-16 from `go test -count=1 -v -skip '^TestAESCipherReorderingTLS13$'
# ./...` on macOS arm64 with Go 1.26 and OpenSSL 3.6.4. The reference peer's bytes
# are environment-specific, so a GitHub ubuntu-latest run can differ by a name or
# two; when the gate says "new test failures" and the reason is a `mismatch on read`
# of a recorded flow, the fix is to add that name here, not to touch the handshake.
#
# Sorted, one name per line; blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored.
